---
title: "Sensors & Channel Authority"
---

## ToF channels

Four VL53L5CX sensors mount on the arm. Each returns an 8x8 distance grid at up to 15 Hz. The `safety/` stack treats channels as one of three authorities:

| Channel | Location | Authority | Rationale |
|---------|----------|-----------|-----------|
| CH0 | Front / side | Primary | Faces the sweep direction. Gates replans and blocks manual input when a valid near-return appears. |
| CH1 | Back / side | Primary | Covers the opposite side of the sweep. Same gating as CH0. |
| CH2 | Top / side | Primary | Promoted from advisory on 2026-04-10 after a hardware test: a user held a hand close to the sensor and the arm continued to sweep through it because CH2 was classified as advisory. Every working ToF channel now holds replan authority by default. |
| CH3 | Bottom | Ignored | Points at the floor. Near-returns are dominated by ground reflections and produce constant false positives. |

The rule is encoded in `braccio_main_runner/braccio_ctrl/constants.py`:

```python
SENSOR_REPLAN_CHANNELS   = [0, 1, 2]
SENSOR_ADVISORY_CHANNELS = []
SENSOR_IGNORE_CHANNELS   = [3]
```

## Per-channel distance thresholds

```python
TOF_THRESHOLDS_MM = [250.0, 250.0, 250.0, 50.0]
```

A channel reports an obstacle response when any pixel in the 8x8 grid has a valid target return closer than the threshold. CH3's 50 mm threshold is effectively unreachable from the arm's normal envelope, matching the "ignore" classification above.

## ToF frame format

The Teensy publishes each frame as:

```
TF,<seq>,<ms>,S<ch>,<ch>,<joint>,<status>,<rows>,<cols>,<d0..dN>,<v0..vN>
```

`<status>` is the VL53L5CX target_status code. `<d0..dN>` are 64 distances in millimetres; `<v0..vN>` are 64 validity flags. The `tof_sensor.ToFBridge` parser validates each pixel by status code and exposes a `diag_masked_cells` field so the safety stack can distinguish genuine near-returns from occluded pixels.

## IR severity encoding

Four IR sensors each produce a binary signal. A count of firing sensors maps to severity:

| Firing sensors | Severity | Label |
|-----:|------|-------|
| 0 | 0 | CLEAR |
| 1 | 1 | FAR |
| 2 | 2 | CLOSE |
| 3+ | 3 | DANGER |

The firmware sends the severity directly as `IR,<0-3>`. The controller maps severity 2 or higher to a reactive retreat.

## IMU

The MPU-6050 posts roll and pitch from the accelerometer at 10 Hz. Yaw is not fused because the MPU-6050 lacks a magnetometer; absolute heading comes from encoder feedback on the base servo. The IMU's rotation matrix is cached in `imu_state.py` and invalidated only when roll, pitch, or the user-calibrated yaw reference changes.
